paper_title: Photoluminescence spectroscopy of dibenzopentacene single-crystals: multiple emissive states across temperature, time, and magnetic field in a pursuit of exothermic singlet fission

knowledge_points.content: 1,2;8,9-dibenzopentacene (DBP) single crystals pack in the P21212 space group with a herringbone arrangement, where each molecule has six nearest neighbors and three types of intermolecular contacts within the ac plane.
knowledge_points.evidence: The unit cell contains four symmetry-equivalent DBP molecules (space group P21212, Fig. 1b). The molecules are packed in layers parallel to the ac plane with a herringbone arrangement in each layer so that each DBP molecule has 6 close neighbors and three types of DBP-DBP intermolecular contacts in the layer.

knowledge_points.content: The lowest-energy S0-S1 absorption transition in DBP single crystals is shifted to 2.09 eV, representing a 0.25 eV redshift compared to the solution phase due to intermolecular interactions.
knowledge_points.evidence: In crystalline DBP, intermolecular interactions shift the S0-S1 excitation to lower energy by 0.25 eV. Furthermore, the DBP single crystal shows strongly polarized absorption with well-resolved Davydov splitting... The more intense Davydov component with the maximum at 2.09 eV is polarized parallel to the a direction.

knowledge_points.content: DBP single crystals exhibit five co-existing and interconverting emissive states (I-V), where free excitons (State I) dominate below 20 K and convert to self-trapped excitons (STEs) at higher temperatures.
knowledge_points.evidence: A complex evolution of excitation was found between 5 and 300 K, with in total five co-existing and interconverting emissive states. Free excitons dominate the PL spectra below 20 K, but then convert to self-trapped excitons (STEs) at higher temperatures.

knowledge_points.content: The interconversion between free excitons (State I) and self-trapped excitons (State II/III) in DBP is thermally activated with a calculated activation barrier of 6.5 meV (52 cm⁻¹).
knowledge_points.evidence: The fast drop of the intensity of state I with temperature... points to the thermally activated mechanism (Fig. S7a, ESI†). Fitting the linear part gives the activation barrier of 6.5 meV (52 cm⁻¹).

knowledge_points.content: State II in DBP single crystals is characterized by a 0-0 transition at 2.04 eV (608 nm) and converts into State III with a thermal activation barrier of 16 meV (128 cm⁻¹).
knowledge_points.evidence: The spectrum of state II... has a 0–0 transition at 608 nm (2.04 eV)... the quenching of state II can be described as a thermally activated conversion into state III with the barrier of 16 meV (128 cm⁻¹).

knowledge_points.content: The photoluminescence intensity of DBP single crystals decreases by approximately 20-fold between 120 K and room temperature, a phenomenon attributed to the onset of singlet fission.
knowledge_points.evidence: A 20-fold decrease of the PL intensity between 120 K and room temperature is ascribed to the singlet fission, which is confirmed by magneto-PL measurements.

knowledge_points.content: At room temperature, DBP single crystals exhibit classical Merrifield signatures of singlet fission, characterized by a PL intensity decrease of 1.5% at 0.02 T followed by an increase of 4% at 0.2 T.
knowledge_points.evidence: By 300 K, the transition to the new regime is complete... the (T1...T1)-specific PLH/PL0 behavior with a negative dip of -1.5% at 0.02 T followed by a growth to +4% at 0.2 T becomes much more pronounced.

knowledge_points.content: All emissive states in DBP single crystals are polarized along the 'a' crystallographic axis, matching the polarization of the lowest-energy Davydov component in the absorption spectrum.
knowledge_points.evidence: At all temperatures and all wavelengths, emission is polarized along the a crystallographic axis. This corresponds to the polarization of the lowest-energy Davydov component in the absorption spectra.

knowledge_points.content: State IV in DBP crystals is a long-lived emissive state with a 0-0 transition at 1.81 eV (687 nm) and a lifetime of 19 ns at 200 K, which shortens to 8 ns at 300 K.
knowledge_points.evidence: In addition to the 0–0 transition at 687 nm (1.81 eV), state IV also has a broadened vibronic peak at 750 nm... The lifetime of state IV at 200 K is 19 ns... shortened gradually from 19 ns at 200 K to 8 ns at 300 K.

knowledge_points.content: The quenching of State III above 140 K is a thermally activated process with a barrier of 63 meV (509 cm⁻¹), potentially leading to a non-radiative channel or conversion to State IV.
knowledge_points.evidence: The quenching of state III between 140 and 200 K can be described as a thermally-activated process with the barrier of 63 meV (509 cm⁻¹). However, it is not a conversion into another bright state... either it can be a conversion into state IV... or a new non-radiative channel is open.

knowledge_points.content: DBP exhibits enhanced photo and air stability compared to pentacene, making it a robust candidate for studying acene-based photophysics.
knowledge_points.evidence: 1,2;8,9-dibenzopentacene (DBP hereafter...)... managed to avoid attention despite its availability as an unsubstituted PAH and enhanced photo and air stability in comparison to pentacene.
